carrier.homoglyph.name: Homoglyph substitution
carrier.homoglyph.note: Substitutes look-alike letters. Survives copy and paste and PDF rendering. Detectable at any density.
carrier.zero_width.name: Zero-width characters
carrier.zero_width.note: Inserts invisible characters between visible ones. Highest capacity, no length limit.
carrier.whitespace_var.name: Whitespace variation
carrier.whitespace_var.note: Uses an invisible spacing channel distinct from the zero-width one. Needs about nine cover characters per payload byte.
carrier.bidi.name: Bidirectional controls
carrier.bidi.note: Uses direction control characters. Needs about nine cover characters per payload byte. Removed by aggressive sanitizers.
cipher.none.name: No encryption
cipher.none.note: The layer is embedded as plain bytes. Anyone who finds it can read it.
cipher.recipient_pqc.name: Recipient (post-quantum)
cipher.recipient_pqc.note: The secret is sealed to a recipient's public key before it is hidden. Only their secret key opens it, and there is no shared passphrase.
compose.recipient.label: Recipient public key
compose.recipient.hint: The recipient generates a key pair in the Decode tab and shares the public half. Their secret half opens what you seal here.
compose.recipient.measure_note: Recipient sealing adds a fixed post-quantum overhead this preview does not size. The exact capacity is checked when you compose.
compose.recipient.file_unsupported: Recipient sealing is not available on a loaded file yet. Use the pasted-text path to seal to a recipient.

compose.title: Compose
compose.intro: Place a hidden layer inside a cover text. The visible result is the complete cover text, unchanged to the reader.
compose.content.title: Content
compose.encryption.title: Encryption
compose.secret.label: Text to hide
compose.secret.placeholder: The message that will travel inside the cover text
compose.cover.label: Cover text
compose.cover.placeholder: The visible text that carries the hidden layer
compose.cover.file.label: Or hide inside a file
compose.cover.file.hint: Pick a document or drop one on the box above. The secret is hidden inside that file, and the marked file downloads in its original format. A container or web document is refused by name.
compose.carriers.label: Carriers
compose.carriers.hint: Select one or more. Each selected carrier receives a full copy of the hidden layer, so any single surviving carrier is enough to recover it.
compose.carriers.read_path_broken_detail: This carrier can be applied, and the mark it leaves is real, but the engine cannot currently read the layer back from it on a cover text longer than the payload. Combine it with a carrier that reads back, or select it only to leave a mark. The state shown here is measured at startup, not declared, so it will change on its own when the engine changes.
compose.carriers.invalid_combination: This combination is refused by the engine.
compose.cipher.label: Encryption
compose.cipher.hint: Applied to the hidden layer before it is placed in the cover text.
compose.password.label: Passphrase
compose.password.placeholder: Required when an encryption method is selected
compose.capacity.title: Capacity
compose.capacity.conservative_note: Availability is measured against the cover text as typed. When several carriers are combined, later carriers see a longer text and gain capacity, so this figure is a lower bound.
compose.result.title: Result
compose.result.hint: This is the complete cover text. Copy it as it is; reformatting or retyping destroys the hidden layer.
compose.error.no_password: Enter a passphrase, or set encryption to none.
compose.mission.title: Mission
compose.mission.hint: Choose what the hidden layer is for. The mission sets a recommended density, and the slider shows how much fits and how visible it becomes on this cover text.
compose.mission.density.label: Density
compose.mission.overflow: This much cannot be concealed on this cover text: it needs {needed} bits, and the mission budget here is {available} bits.
compose.recommend.hint: Weigh every carrier and mission for this secret and cover, then apply the most discreet setting that holds it without overflow.
compose.recommend.nofit: No setting hides this without overflow on this cover text. It is short by {shortfall} bytes: use a longer cover, a smaller secret, or a looser mission.
compose.recommend.empty: Enter a cover text and a secret first, then ask for a recommendation.
compose.frame.robust.label: Robust frame
compose.frame.robust.hint: Off by default. The light frame carries text in short covers. The robust frame adds recovery markers so a partly damaged or excerpted document can still be read, and it needs more room for the same secret.
compose.saturate.label: Saturation
compose.saturate.hint: Off by default. The aggressive variant: it fills each carrier's channel with the secret repeated, so the mark saturates the text and survives a heavy cut. The visible text is unchanged and the secret still reads back. It overrides the robust frame.
compose.payload.title: Payload
compose.payload.hint: Hide a small file inside the cover text, on its own or alongside the text above. You can make the file smaller before it is hidden.

compose.payload.file.hint: Choose a small file. Its bytes are read locally and are not sent anywhere. The size limit is set by the engine, which refuses a file that is too large by name.

compose.payload.attach: Add to the text to hide

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.intro: Attach a signed provenance record to a document, or verify one you received. The tool marks and verifies; the legal obligation itself sits with AI providers and deployers, not with the tool.
provenance.disclaimer: This enables Article 50 aligned marking and verification. It is a marking and detection tool, not a compliance certificate and not an evasion tool.
provenance.assertion.human_authorship.no: States that the holder of the signing key authored this text.
provenance.assertion.ai_generated.name: AI generated
provenance.assertion.ai_generated.note: Discloses that the text was produced by an AI system, the Article 50 disclosure use. Sign it with a pipeline key, distinct from a human authorship key.
provenance.assertion.integrity.name: Integrity
provenance.assertion.integrity.note: Carries the document hash so any later alteration is detectable.
provenance.assertion.recipient_fingerpri: Ties this copy to one recipient, so a leaked copy can be traced back to who received it.
provenance.binding.detached.name: Detached sidecar
provenance.binding.detached.note: A record kept in a separate file beside the text. Survives any change to the text while it is kept, nothing once it is lost.
provenance.binding.in_band.name: In-band mark
provenance.binding.in_band.note: Woven into the text through a carrier. Survives copy and paste, not a determined strip or a rewrite. The realised strength is measured on the produced text.
provenance.identity.title: Signing identity
provenance.identity.intro: Generate an Ed25519 key pair to sign with. Keep the private key secret: anyone who holds it can sign in your name. The public key is safe to publish so others can verify your marks.
provenance.identity.private_warning: Copy the private key now and store it safely. It is shown once, never saved by this application, and never written to a log.

canary.title: Canary trap
canary.intro: Give each recipient a copy that looks identical but carries an invisible, per-recipient mark. If a copy leaks, trace it back to the recipient it was issued to.
canary.disclaimer: The mark survives copy and paste, printing and PDF export. It does not survive a recipient who retypes or rewrites the text from scratch. This identifies who forwarded a copy, not who rekeyed it by hand.
canary.generate.title: Generate marked copies
canary.generate.intro: One document, one recipient per line, and a per-document salt. Each recipient gets a copy that reads exactly like the original.

canary.generate.document.placeholder: The text to issue to each recipient

canary.generate.recipients.hint: A name, an email or a reference. Each line receives its own marked copy.
canary.generate.salt.label: Salt
canary.generate.salt.hint: Use a different salt per document, so a recipient's mark does not repeat from one document to the next.
canary.generate.error.no_recipients: Name at least one recipient, one per line.
canary.generate.result.title: Marked copies
canary.generate.result.cover_restored_ok: Every copy strips back to the original text exactly, so all copies look identical.
canary.generate.result.cover_restored_fa: A copy does not strip back to the original text. Do not distribute this result.
canary.generate.result.registry_hint: Save this and keep it. It is what identifies a leak later. Without it, a leaked copy cannot be traced.
canary.generate.result.versions_hint: Hand each recipient their own copy. Copy it as it is; retyping destroys the mark.

about.title: About
about.product.title: The application
about.product.body: SteganoHero is a private laboratory for text provenance and traceability. It composes documents that carry information about their own origin, and it inspects received documents for the same. Everything runs on the local machine. No text, passphrase or key leaves it.
about.capabilities.title: What it can do
about.capabilities.item1: Compose a document that carries an additional layer of information, invisible in normal reading, leaving the visible text intact.
about.capabilities.item2: Protect that layer with a passphrase, so that only the intended reader can recover it.
about.capabilities.item3: Recover the layer from a received document and report whether it arrived intact.
about.capabilities.item4: Inspect any document and report whether it carries such a layer, with a confidence assessment and a full character-level breakdown.
about.capabilities.item5: Measure what changed between an original document and a copy that came back.
about.publisher.title: Hope 'n Mind
about.publisher.body: An independent research holding, active since 2006, dedicated to the resilience and stability of complex systems.
about.mission.title: Mission
about.mission.intro: Fundamental research that contributes to civilizational stability, along five lines.
about.mission.item1: Metrology and analysis of systemic coherence.
about.mission.item3: Rehabilitation of the economic and social fabric.
about.vision.title: Vision
about.vision.body: Preparing civilizational transitions on a century scale, while maintaining social peace and systemic stability. The work is not done for ourselves, but for those who come after.
about.record.title: Record
about.record.body: Twenty years of research in systemic architecture and resilience: coherence metrology, interactions inside complex systems, resilience frameworks, long-term stability models, and the maintenance of social peace.
about.ethics.title: Ethical commitment
about.ethics.quote: Mastery of knowledge imposes an ethics of restraint, for the benefit of social cohesion.
about.ethics.body: This laboratory is held to that commitment. Its capabilities are described by what they achieve, never by how they achieve it.
about.contact.title: Contact
about.contact.body: Open to constructive exchange and to ethical partnerships that serve systemic stability.
about.build.title: Build
about.legal.notice: Private laboratory software. Not distributed publicly.
airegulation.title: AI-regulation
airegulation.intro: See the marks your own document carries, remove the ones you choose, and read the content credential a file declares. This is about your own content, never about defeating another party's detection.
airegulation.disclaimer: This works on documents you hold. It removes the mark classes named below and reports what it leaves behind. It does not remove statistical or token-sampling watermarks, and it never claims a document is unmarked beyond the classes it acted on.
airegulation.wordmark.group.title: Word-choice marks
airegulation.wordmark.group.intro: Marks that live in the choice of words, not in the characters or the metadata. These modules analyze and perturb them, and state plainly the limit they cannot pass.
airegulation.wordmark.analyze.title: Analyze word choices
airegulation.wordmark.analyze.intro: Read a text for marks carried in the choice of words, with a certainty on each finding.
airegulation.wordmark.analyze.text.label: Text
airegulation.wordmark.analyze.acrostic.p: A word you suspect is hidden in the initials.
airegulation.wordmark.analyze.key.label: Your own key in hex (optional)

airegulation.wordmark.analyze.result.emp: No findings beyond the structural limit.
airegulation.wordmark.scrub.title: Perturb word choices
airegulation.wordmark.scrub.intro: Change synonym choices locally to disrupt a word-choice mark. Best-effort, not a removal, and nothing is sent anywhere.
airegulation.wordmark.scrub.text.label: Text
airegulation.wordmark.scrub.result.title: Result
airegulation.wordmark.scrub.result.note: This is a best-effort local disruption by changing synonym choices. It is not a removal and makes no guarantee: a word-choice watermark can only be reduced by rewriting.
airegulation.wordmark.rewrite.title: Rewrite to reduce a word-choice mark
airegulation.wordmark.rewrite.intro: Rewrite the text with a model to disrupt a word-choice mark. A local server (Ollama, LM Studio) keeps everything on your machine; an online endpoint shows a disclaimer first.
airegulation.wordmark.rewrite.model.plac: The model to use, for example a local instruct model.
airegulation.wordmark.rewrite.text.label: Text

airegulation.wordmark.rewrite.result.rec: The rewritten text was re-cleaned locally of any freshly added character marks.
airegulation.wordmark.binoculars.title: AI-origin (Binoculars)
airegulation.wordmark.binoculars.intro: Score a text with two local models to estimate whether a model generated it. Probable, never proof, and it needs a matched model pair to be calibrated.
airegulation.wordmark.binoculars.unavail: This module needs the embedded model, which is not included in this build.
airegulation.wordmark.binoculars.observe: Path to a local GGUF model.
airegulation.wordmark.binoculars.perform: Path to a second local GGUF model.
A lower score leans machine-generated. This is a probable signal, not proof; calibrated detection needs a matched model pair.

airegulation.pristine.title: Pristine clean
airegulation.pristine.intro: Return a document you hold to a pristine state. This removes every mark class and every remaining invisible or format-control character, so the text re-analyses as fully clean. The visible words are kept.
airegulation.pristine.tradeoff: This is a declared, opt-in mode. It also removes invisibles that can carry meaning (for example an emoji joiner, a right-to-left run, an Arabic or Indic joiner), so any text that relied on them will render differently. Use it only when you want a fully clean result and accept that change. For a lighter clean that keeps meaning-bearing invisibles, use Clean above.

files.title: Files
files.intro: Run the safe document tools on a real file you hold: see the marks it carries, and remove the ones you choose, written back in the file's own format. This is about your own content, never about defeating another party's detection.
files.disclaimer: This works on documents you hold: Word (.docx), OpenDocument (.odt), HTML, Markdown, and plain text. It removes the mark classes you tick and reports what it leaves behind. Where a format cannot be cleaned without loss, it says so by name rather than returning a partial file.
wordmark.online.title: Before an online rewrite
wordmark.online.disclaimer: This step sends your text to an external service you chose. Use it on files you hold, for your own private and offline use, not for online redistribution. A watermark that lives in the choice of words can only be reduced by rewriting, which changes the text and carries no guarantee. You stay responsible for how you use the result.

files.clean.result.residual_label: What this clean does not cover
files.clean.result.download_hint: Saves the cleaned document in its original format.
files.clean.result.container_note: This format keeps its structure, so the cleaned result is the saved file, not a text preview.
files.strip.title: Strip metadata
files.strip.intro: Remove the metadata the picked file carries (author, tool, timestamps and similar fields), written back in the file's own format. The visible content is left byte for byte identical. A format that has no metadata surface is refused by its name.
files.strip.result.title: Strip result
files.strip.result.altered: Metadata was removed. The content is unchanged, and the file keeps its original format.
files.strip.result.unaltered: Nothing changed. This file carried no metadata to remove.
files.strip.download_hint: Saves the file with its metadata removed, in its original format.
files.pristine.title: Pristine clean
files.pristine.intro: Return the picked file to a pristine state. This removes every mark class and every remaining invisible or format-control character, so the content re-analyses as fully clean, written back in the file's own format. The visible words are kept. A container or web-markup format is refused by its name.
files.pristine.tradeoff: This is a declared, opt-in mode. It also removes invisibles that can carry meaning (for example an emoji joiner, a right-to-left run, an Arabic or Indic joiner), so any text that relied on them will render differently. Use it only when you want a fully clean result and accept that change. For a lighter clean that keeps meaning-bearing invisibles, use Clean above.
files.pristine.result.title: Pristine result
files.pristine.result.altered: The file was returned to a pristine state. What was removed is listed below.
files.pristine.result.unaltered: Nothing changed. The file already held no mark class and no invisible character.
files.pristine.result.notes_label: What this pristine clean did, and its trade-off
files.pristine.download_hint: Saves the pristine file in its original format.
decoder.title: Traced reveal
decoder.intro: Recover a payload from a received text and see the wave trace that shows how it was recovered, layer by layer, with each layer's verdict. The trace is the artefact: a failure is a location, not a bare error.
decoder.text.label: Received text
decoder.file.label: Or a marked document file
decoder.file.hint: Pick a file to read its marked text back instead of pasting it.
decoder.text.placeholder: Paste the text exactly as received
decoder.password.label: Passphrase
decoder.password.placeholder: Leave empty if the payload was not encrypted
decoder.password.hint: The tab never asks which method was used. Recovery is driven by what the document records, not by guessing.
decoder.recovery.label: Allow recovery mode
decoder.recovery.hint: Off by default. When a document carries no header, recovery reads an older-format or fragment document. It is never entered on its own, and the result names it when it runs.
decoder.recovery.prompt: No document header was found. This may be a fragment, or an older-format document. Allow recovery mode and reveal again to read it.
decoder.payload.title: Payload
decoder.payload.binary: Binary payload, not shown as text:
decoder.integrity.verified: An exact check verified this payload.
decoder.integrity.unverified: No exact check verified this payload.
decoder.trace.title: Wave trace
decoder.trace.intro: Each layer is reverted in strict reverse order, one wave per layer. The wave that stops the chain names itself, and nothing after it is reached.
decoder.trace.undetermined: No readable layer was found. This is undetermined, not a failure.
decoder.oracle.legend_exact: A solid marker is an exact, recorded verdict: an authentication tag or a checksum confirmed this layer.
decoder.oracle.legend_probabilistic: A striped marker is a score, not a proof: a statistical reading, shown as a likelihood and never as a certainty.
decoder.oracle.legend_undetermined: A hollow marker is undetermined: nothing here could be checked, which is not the same as a failure.
settings.title: Engine settings
settings.intro: The runtime configuration this tool exposes: the per-purpose planning densities and the key-derivation parameters. Every change is checked by the engine before it is stored: a value outside its accepted range is refused by name, never quietly adjusted.
settings.scope.title: Where these apply
settings.scope.body: These are the engine's runtime configuration values. A change is validated and stored for this session; it is not saved to disk, so at the next start the engine returns to its defaults. The interface language and theme are set in the header and are remembered separately.
settings.density.title: Planning density
settings.density.intro: How much of a document's available room each purpose plans to use. A lower value keeps a mark less noticeable, a higher value plans for more at the cost of how visible it may be. The engine still measures and enforces the real capacity of each document; this only sets what is planned for. Each purpose has its own accepted range.
settings.density.conceal.label: Conceal
settings.density.conceal.hint: The share planned when the goal is to stay unnoticed.
settings.density.sign.label: Sign
settings.density.sign.hint: The share planned when attributing a document.
settings.density.mark.label: Mark
settings.density.mark.hint: The share planned when marking copies so they can be traced.
settings.crypto.title: Passphrase protection
settings.crypto.intro: The key-derivation parameters this tool exposes: the memory, passes, and threads configured for turning a passphrase into a key. Higher memory and more passes mean stronger, slower derivation.
settings.crypto.memory.label: Memory
settings.crypto.memory.hint: Memory configured for key derivation, in kibibytes. Higher means stronger and slower.
settings.crypto.passes.label: Passes
settings.crypto.passes.hint: Passes configured over that memory. Higher means stronger and slower.
settings.crypto.parallelism.label: Threads
settings.crypto.parallelism.hint: Threads the derivation is configured to use.
settings.crypto.cipher.label: Default confidentiality layer
settings.crypto.cipher.hint: Offered when a document does not name one. Choose none to default to no confidentiality layer.
settings.result.title: In effect now
settings.result.intro: The configuration the engine reports it is holding, read back after the last change. This is what is stored, not merely what was typed.
settings.result.applied: Changes applied. The stored configuration now holds the values below.
